name: Rajput Garasia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Phillips, Maxwell P. 2012. Dialect continuum in the Bhil tribal belt: grammatical aspects. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Modern comparative study of Bhil-belt varieties with a phonological overview; need to check whether a Garasia (Sirohi/Danta) sample point is included and whether prosody is remarked on. Open access in principle but could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Vyas, Yogendra D. 1967. A linguistic study of Bhili dialects: a descriptive study of Central and North Bhili. PhD thesis, Gujarat University. (Central Bhili = Sukhsar/Jhalod, Panch Mahals; 'North Bhili' = Dungarpur area, i.e. Wagdi country — NOT Rajput Garasia; read only as areal context.)
sources.note: For both varieties: 'Stress is not distinctive. Syllable division can be made in terms of phonetic criteria.' (thesis pp. 28, 133). Not applicable to rajp1235 (different varieties: Panchmahals Bhili and Dungarpur Wagdi).

sources.citation: Ashok Kumar. 2023. Garasiya gaur [The Garasia Gaur festival]. GAP Bhasha 4(3): 58-66. In Hindi (Siyawa, Abu Road, Sirohi).
sources.note: Silent; ethnographic, only mentions that the tribe has its own 'Girasi' boli.

sources.citation: Cain, Bruce D. (comp.). 2013. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Garasia Dialects. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-014. Dallas: SIL International. iii+50 pp. (fieldwork 1987-88; Rajput Garasia sites Dhabaavalivav-Danta, Kui-Abu Road, Mama Pipla-Khedbrahma, Piplo-Bali).
sources.note: Silent. Lexical similarity, recorded-text intelligibility, bilingualism, language use/attitudes only; the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2011. Linguistic Survey of India: Rajasthan, Part I. Kolkata. (Wagdi chapter only; intro p. iv notes 'Besides Wagdi, Garasia Bhili and Baori.. speakers are found in Rajasthan in good number', i.e. Garasia not yet surveyed.)
sources.note: Nothing on Garasia; the Wagdi and Marwari sketches treat only nasalisation under suprasegmentals.

sources.citation: Lal, R. B. 1979. Sons of the Aravalli: The Garasias. Ahmedabad: Tribal Research and Training Institute, Gujarat Vidyapith. Section 'Language of the Garasias' (p. 29).
sources.note: Silent. One paragraph: a Bhili dialect with Marwari influence, locally 'Nyar-ki-boli' / 'Magra-ki-boli'.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX: Indo-Aryan family, Central group, Part III: The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Girasia or Nyar' dialect note and specimens (Jodhpur-Marwar; Sirohi State), printed pp. 26-29.
sources.note: Silent. The Girasia/Nyar note only remarks on e for other vowels, dental l for cerebral l, Marwari genitive -ro, and Marwari admixture; the only accent remark in the volume is the survey-wide transliteration convention (acute marks an accented syllable when needed).

sources.citation: Shekhawat, Arjun Singh. [2000s]. Bhakhar ra bhomiya (Adivasi Garasiya sahitya). New Delhi: Sahitya Akademi. In Hindi/Rajasthani; Sirohi-Abu Garasia oral literature; chapter 'Bhasha aur Garasi boli'.
sources.note: Silent. Notes only segmental correspondences vs Hindi/Rajasthani (s>h, c>s, initial vowel changes, vowel-length differences) and states that no grammar of the Garasi boli has been. no balaghat/svaraghat term anywhere.

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. (chief ed.); Kanji Patel (ed.). 2022. The Languages of Gujarat, Diu & Daman and Dadra & Nagar Haveli (PLSI vol. 9 pt. 2). Orient BlackSwan. Ch. 18 'Garasia' (and ch. 16 'Dungri Bhili').

sources.note: Only recent published sketch titled 'Garasia' (Gujarat side: Banaskantha/Sabarkantha, where both Rajput and Adiwasi Garasia live); PLSI entries sometimes include a brief phonology note. Need to check which Garasia it describes and whether stress is mentioned.

sources.note: LSI state volumes carry a 'suprasegmental phonemes' section per mother tongue; a Garasia chapter would be the natural modern primary source.

sources.citation: Unpublished SIL / Indian Evangelical Mission phonology write-up for Rajput Garasia by Victoria Williams (Patel), 1980s, underlying the Rajput Garasia literacy and scripture work referred to in Cain 2013's preface ('Mrs. Patel whose extensive field work and previous surveys laid the foundation').
